headline: Walmart and drone company Wing plan to start delivering orders by drone in Denver and Seattle in 2027, adding to the five metro areas already served.
score_reason: Kept at the pool score: a real expansion of a drone delivery service already running in five metro areas, but the new cities are a plan for 2027.
importance_line: Shoppers in the Denver and Seattle areas could get drone delivery from Walmart stores from 2027, but it is an announced plan, only eligible orders will qualify and the drones carry up to five pounds.
summary: Engadget reports that Walmart and Alphabet-owned drone delivery firm Wing plan to start operations in the Denver and Seattle areas in 2027, as part of a plan to offer air delivery from more than 270 Walmart stores across the US. The service now runs in five metro areas (Atlanta, Charlotte, Dallas–Fort Worth, Houston and Orlando), its drones fly at up to 60 mph and carry up to five pounds, and eligible Walmart orders show drone delivery as an option in the app or on the website.
notes: Read in full (a short Engadget text). Status REPORTED because Engadget relays the companies' announcement without quoting either of them. The drones already deliver in five metro areas, which is the machine action; the new part is the 2027 plan. Engadget says the pair aim to reach fourteen other destinations but does not say whether Denver and Seattle are among them, so that count is left out.
